text:
Have been to the Edmonton City Center location a few times and as I usually go mid afternoon it's often not too busy. The service has been very good and quite fast with the servers being friendly and helpful. 

I like the poutine and the fries by themselves are acceptable though not crazy good. The Fatburger as its called is a decent size (esp when paired with the poutine) but I agree with some other reviewers that there's nothing about the taste of the burger that says "Fatburger". I mean to say that there's nothing distinctive about it. You'll never mistake a Big Mac for a Great Canadian or Whopper. They do a great job at branding their image and should brand their taste in the same way. Blindfolded, most would be hard pressed to say what establishment made their burger when eating here.

The noise level when I go has been middle level and was easy to carry a conversation. Their milkshakes are good too! Price wise it thought it reasonable with a burger + drink + poutine coming in around $15. Overall, I've had good times and would go back.

Just about noon on a weekday and I thought this place would be packed.  It wasn't and we were able to snag the last U booth, although there were still tables available.  I didn't want to have a meal leaving me too full before a meeting so I had a turkey burger with no sides.  We waited about 10 minutes for our meals, and my friend got his beef burger before mine.

The turkey burger had cranberry, tomato, lettuce, and mayo.  It was tasty but not amazing and usually they put too much mayo for my liking.  I should have asked light on the mayo.  One of the staff came to check on us during our meal which was unexpected service.  She was also prompt taking away our empty trays after we were finished.

Burger was alright for almost $9 but there are better places to eat for a lunch date.

Fatburger is one of those so so places that if your friends suggest it to you during a day of shopping your not going to have any objections but at the same time it's likely something you would not actively seek out on your own.

The burgers here are good although the patties I find are a bit on the thin side. They come out very flavorful thankfully and in all my times eating here I have never had an issue with a burger being overdone. They always seem to have fresh ingredients as well which I can appreciate as runny tomatoes and wilted lettuce are big sins in my book. Fries have always been on the crispier side on all my visits which is great for me as that is how I like mine done but if you don't like a bit of a crunch with your fries your likely to take issue.

They do offer some other things on the menu as well but I recommend sticking to the burgers. On one visit I had the chicken Caesar salad and the lettuce and chicken appeared to be drowning in a lake of dressing. 

Wait times here for me have averaged about 10-15 minutes which I think is alright considering they are a notch above typical fast food. Refills on pop are free and they have a pretty good selection available but they don't let you pump your own ketchup which is a pet peeve of mine as I love ketchup. This place isn't fantastic but it isn't bad and it's definitely one of the better spots to sit down and grab a bite in City Center

I don't do negative reviews that often. I've tried this place several times though, and each time I get the same service, and poor quality food. The order taker doesn't offer suggestions at the till, simply points up to the menu and stares expectantly at you. I get that they are trying to streamline, but still, a little help or selling of the daily special would go a long way in helping to choose from all the options listed. I don't like pre-tipping either... not going to buy into it!  My last visit involved the "Hawaiian burger" it was literally a regular burger smothered in teryaki sauce and a cold pineapple ring slapped on a bun with mayo and lettuce, the value isn't there, neither is the quality. Really don't think I want to try this place again.

Bought a groupon coupon for two cheeseburgers and skinny fries for $14 and decided to go to this downtown location.  It was around 1:15 on a Sunday afternoon and was not busy, about 4 tables taken.  The manager took my order and was very quick.

The menu is quite large ranging from beef burgers, chicken, turkey, veggie and fish burgers, poutine, milkshakes, dessert and even alcohol.  You can choose from various toppings for your burger such as the regular stuff like relish, mustard, lettuce, tomato but there is also grilled onions, bbq sauce, deli pickle, banana peppers and ranch dressing.  For an extra $1.19 you can choose different cheese, a fried egg, onion ring, guacamole and a few other choices.

The burgers are made fresh so there is about a 6 to 8 minute wait.  While waiting, you can see the staff hard at work getting the orders out.  The cheeseburgers were huge and the patty was thick and juicy.  It was really tasty especially with my topping choices (love the bbq sauce and banana peppers).  Be prepared, it will be messy!  The fries were crispy and cooked just right.  The burgers here taste and look better than fast food at McDonald's or Dairy Queen.

I hear the milkshakes are really good so for sure, we will be back to try one and most likely another burger!

I'm on my honeymoon, I've been in Alberta for a week. I'm tired of A&W. I was so excited when I saw fat burger in the food court at west ed. Unfortunately the wait was so long that we opt'd out for Harvey's. I hope my wife doesn't leave me.

Fatburger has always been one of those places in California you hear about as a must for burgers. Thus part of me was excited (it happens sometimes) when I stumbled upon the chain near the pedway entrance to Churchill station from City Centre mall. Right next to the mammoth Christmas tree on display.

Walking in one gets a real polished vibe. It appears somebody thoroughly enjoys deep, shinny reds, reflection-baring blacks, corrugated metal and some neon signs thrown in for good luck. One would figure this wouldn't work on paper, but it's lovely inside particularly if one enjoys a commercialized version of a 50's diner. 

After working with an auctioneer style of order taker, the California burger ($7.99) and yam fries ($4.99) called to me. The burger was good, but lacked any kind of wow factor. Though lack of "wow" is by no means a technical description, lets just say I am having trouble understanding why I would go out of my way to seek a Fatburger save convenience. 

With such an influx of restaurants in the biz of putting out premium burgers, one really need to grab the customer's attention. Why not focus on making a killer guacamole spread for the Californian to give it some pop. It wasn't bad, I just expected more.

A strange start to a Saturday morning.Early wake then fat burger and casino before noon. Wow!

I had a rough Friday night, and woke up really early on Saturday which almost never happens.  I decided to be efficient and went grocery shopping to save on foods at 8:30 am which I have not done before. There are only 3 people  that morning at save on foods shopping, mainly couples and families.

I got super hungry early, and went downtown to grab some food. I wanted, no I needed a big burger so I went to fat burger in city centre. Amazingly I was not alone 8 or 9 other people were ordering burgers and fries at 10 am. I could of ordered a beer with my meal, but would have probably gotten ill quite fast. Anyway weird start to my morning, so I ordered the double burger with fries, gravy and a pop. My roommate ordered a regular fat burger, fries, gravy and milk shake.

Both meals came to 33.00 and took about 8 minutes, they were cooked just for our order, I watched them take out the frozen burgers and grill them, and cook the  fries. When the burgers arrived they were fresh and very tasty. This is the only burger place that provides you with different seasonings, and sauces to use on your food. The city centre location is very clean and organized. The bathrooms are very modern, and staff all want to keep their jobs. This place is the only place where the staff seem to take their job serious-there is a customer service efficiency to the way they talk with you, and take your order and money!   

Being here so early they had all the brand new editions of newspapers for customers to read, and there are a few small screen monitors to watch shows on TV. The food was fresh and tasty, the burger a little greasy-but had a great grilled flavour, the side gravy was tasty and the french fries were crispy, but not oily for our orders. I couldn't finish my fries or pop, and my roommate couldn't finish his hamburger, or milkshake with out both of us becoming ill. Then it was off to Christmas shopping, and  a short trip over to the local casino to hopefully help pay for some extra Christmas gifts!  The casino is a different story altogether! Most nutritionists only recommend  eating fast food ONCE A MONTH or not at all!!
A nice step up from the awful burgers in the food court.  Mushroom swiss burger loaded, actually overloaded, with great garlicly 'shrooms.

Fatburger, a tip is not part of your expected cash flow - when I pay for an item at your restaurant, I am paying for a service - the food, the atmosphere, and the customer service.  Furthermore, just because a tip is expected does not mean it is earned.  Frankly, the cashier didn't deserve any form of tip - when I asked about the food available, she rudely pointed to the menu above her, and she made no attempt to welcome us to the restaurant.  When my thumb slips entering your tip, and I move to correct it, it is not okay to question me - "are you sure you want to give us such a low tip, sir?" in a surly tone, as happened at Fatburger.  When I correct my tip to 20% on an $11 order, it is unprofessional and frankly, disgusting, that the cashier would then turn and yell to the kitchen staff "Bad tip!" - as happened at Fatburger (Yes, you are expected to tip prior to receiving any form of service here).  Making your customer feel unwelcome will certainly not result in higher profit margins for you and it is never okay to embarrass your customer, as you did me.  In fact, had I not been there with a lady friend - one I wanted to impress, I would have walked out in disgust then and there.

With that said, the burger I had was great, if a little salty.  Since I had a burger with guecomule, I suspected this was the cause of the extra salt.  I couldn't help but wonder though, what else might have made its way into my burger, with the cashier's "bad tip" announcement.  The waitress who came by to check on our meal was very nice, and overall the rest of the experience was quite satisfactory.

Unfortunately, that stunt at the til negatively impacted the entirety of my customer experience, costing you two stars, and as such, I simply can't recommend Fatburger.

To be perfectly honest, finding hamburger downtown at lunch that isn't the typical fast food, is a little challenging.  I was very pleased to find out there was an alternative; Fatburger.

The  50's diner motif, open kitchen, and the wonderful aroma of searing beef, are very impressive upon entering... Until you order, pay, and realize that the "fat burger" isn't really that fat, or particularly special for that matter.  

Sadly nothing about my burger stood out from other burgers.  The patties reminded me of something you would buy from the safeway freezer.  The lettuce was a bottom lump with part of the stem still attached, not a leaf. The tomato was soggy. The bacon was good, I mean for a single strip folded over. The fries didn't stand out. Certainly not worth the almost $20 I paid for my order. 

It was a good meal, but there are better burgers out there for less.

Harvey's
Red Robin's
Hudson's
The Tilted Kilt 
Rodeo Burger
I love the burgers here. I eat here every friday after work and its delicious. Best burger place around the city center area. If you work downtown check this place out for a quick dinner.

I was excited when I saw that a Fatburger was moving into City Center, despite having previously never been to one. When it finally opened, there were lines out the door every day for a couple weeks. Once the lines died down, I decided to give it a try.

You're given a lot of choice, and I had to spend several minutes staring at the menu before I figured out how to simply order a cheeseburger and fries - a little complicated for a glorified fast food joint. The prices were high, meaning that after the first day, this became a very rare lunch destination. 

That said, I love everything here! Their burgers (beef, chicken, or veggie) are all great, their fries are delicious (albeit a little greasy sometimes), and their milkshakes are some of the best I've had. Also, they have free refills on fountain drinks, so I always make sure I stay a little longer and try to get a little bit more out of my money with a refill or two.

The decor is neat, and sitting in the booths near the back it's easy enough to forget you're in a fast food place in a mall. The staff are also friendly and efficient!

Fatburger is a nice occasional indulgence that leaves you feeling a little bit better than a regular fast food binge!

The burger was dry. The bun was cold. 
Very disappointed by this mediocre experience. Would not recommend.

Fatburger is a purveyor of fast food burgers that are definitely a cut above other fast food places. The patty is thin but juicy, and lacks a grilled flavour. The burger gets most of its bite from the added condiments, of which there is a good amount of choice and is very fresh. The bun is also very fresh. With fries and a drink, even with a combo deal, you're almost paying as much as a sit-down restaurant. Definitely check out their shakes, as they are very, very good.

The burgers and fries here taste just like burgers and fries that I would make at home... somewhat average and not that flavourful. I come to a burger place to get a great meal that i could not make myself, and thi splace does not give me that. They have good shakes however.
After writing a complaint to the company they sent me a gift card to retry their downtown location. Definitely a nice gesture and I will be giving them another shot

The food at Fatburger is good but they get one star because fast food should be fast. We had to wait 30 minutes today to get our meals. They said it would be a 10 minute wait which was fine but that turned into 30 minutes. They're was no apology for it taking so long. If my husband hadn't been with me I would have cancelled my order and gotten my money back.

So I came here most recently to while the time away between work and a theatre production and the space was great for that purchase: good fountain beverage options (lemons were available and the lemonade wasn't bad either. Mostly I drank watered down gingerale/lemonade, but the options were good). I liked that staff checked on my sporadically and bussed my table as I finished with things, but didn't mind that I was taking up space as the restaurant wasn't very busy. I read my book and ate my burger and fries and drank my drink.

I was indecisive that day and had ordered the Friday special. I was quite underwhelmed by the burger itself. I don't know what it was about the burger, but it just didn't suit me very well and left me feeling overfull but not pleasantly so. The fries on the otherhand were quite delicious. I liked how they were brought to my table with ample ketchup without my requesting it (and I rarely use ketchup on my fries but it was a nice touch). Good customer service was quite helpful, even if I didn't really appreciate the food itself.
Not memorable and not bad. Fries were ok and food was filling. If I am in the area and hungry I would order, but for the price prefer so many other places like burger priest and A&w even.

Fatburger finally expands to the downtown core. Although it doesn't quite capture the same charm the south side location has created it does do a nice job of creating that old school diner feel.

The menu system is fairly simple: pick a type of burger, the toppings, any additional premium toppings, and optionally upgrade to a combo.
I was fairly confident with my appetite so I decided to man up and order the King Fatty (King sized) with an extra egg with all the fixings. The nice touch that Fatburger provides is they bring the meal out to you like good ol' Dairy Queen.
It wasn't long before I got my meal and right away, grease and fat was just oozing onto the plate. Things to note: the bun looked extremely fresh and moist. My first few bites were a bit disappointing. The burger tasted rather bland. The only distinct taste that stood out were the pickles which gave the burger the familiar tang. As I made my way half way through, I still wasn't tasting anything defining from the burger or patty. The patty actually tasted a little dry and crumbly.
I'm not sure if it was the location or if the quality of the chain has declined but I wasn't floored by the overall taste as when I first discovered Fatburger.

Comparing to a Moxies or a Pub 1905, I would say those burgers would be superior compared to Fatburger. Yes, I would even go to Harvey's (which I think is the best burger for what you're paying for), Dairy Queen, or even A&W for my burger fix.

The King Fatty clocked in at about $9.25 and interestingly enough, you can even get some alcohol with your meal!

As a native Southern Californian, I have fond memories of Fatburger from my youth. I remember the Fatburger as thick and juicy. But the patty I received at the City Centre location was thin, and not particularly juicy, just like almost every other hamburger I've ordered in Canada. I enjoyed the real cheddar and crisp bacon accompaniments, but the grilled onions I requested were not quite grilled enough. I liked the burger, and it certainly beats McDonald's or Burger King, but I prefer Chili's and Red Robin. And the prices are at nearly the Chili's/Red Robin level.

My vegetarian wife ordered a Veggie Burger and we both thought that it contained the most disgusting, rubbery, Veggie patty ever. And Fatburger assumes that you'd like to eat your Veggie Burger on a whole wheat bun just because you're a vegetarian.

While we enjoyed the seasoned salt accompaniment, my wife thought that the french fries tasted as if they were previously frozen.

At a total of $26 for two burgers, an order of fries, a drink, a beer (only $1.99), tax and tip, we thought Fatburger wasn't the best deal.

A couple of friends and I come here once every couple of weeks. 

We are bigger guys and the booths here are terribly uncomfortable. On that alone, I should be giving this place a 3 star review. 

However, the food and service earn back points. 

First, the food. I typically get a small cheeseburger with the works (a preset list of several toppings). I add jalapeños (one of the free additional toppings). I make it a meal with fries and a pop. The burger is prepared reliably well and the fries are always perfectly cooked. A nice touch is the bin of lemon slices that I use to spruce up my pop. My friends are also typically equally happy with the food. 

The service here is the best part. The girls working at this place always do a couple of walk arounds asking how folks are doing. This isn't common in the downtown, lunch rush. I find them genuinely helpful and friendly and they add a nice touch to what would otherwise be a standard eat and leave experience. 

Those booths though; the place is called Fatburger. Give me more room to breathe please.

Located near the 3rd floor food court in City Centre. My wife had the bacon burger. She felt the burger was good - but not as good as the Fatburger in Lethbridge. They don't have gluten free buns in this location. Good choice for a quick burger.
